messages:
alex: heads-up — acme reported a spike of 502/504s hitting the hosted inference API around 08:12 UTC. They see "x-request-id" values and a lot of `upstream timed out` in their gateway logs. sample curl: `curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate`  -> 502.

customer-acme: We started seeing this across multiple routes (chat + embeddings) at ~08:11. Requests that normally complete in <100ms are failing with 502 or hanging until client timeout. Region: us-west-2. We can share traces/ids. :frowning_face:

alex: thanks @customer-acme — can you paste one full response headers/body and the x-request-id? Also any correlation ids from your side. I'll escalate.

customer-acme: here's one header block: `x-request-id: 9f3a2c7b-f1d8-4b1c-8a2a-4d2f3c5b6e7a`, `x-upstream-reason: 502 from control-plane`, body has `{"error":"upstream error"}`. We also saw `error: session lookup timeout` in some responses.

alex: pinging @maya + @ron. This looks like control-plane dependency failures — customers hitting 5xx from hosted inference gateway.

maya: on it. I'm seeing the same x-request-id in our ingress logs. Initial grep shows a cluster of `auth/session` timeouts followed by `routing-policy` 504s.

maya: quick log snippet (from ingress):
```
2026-03-14T08:11:23Z ingress-1 svc gateway request_id=9f3a2c7b route=/v1/generate upstream=control-plane:502 "auth: session lookup timeout"
2026-03-14T08:11:23Z ingress-1 svc gateway request_id=9f3a2c7b route=/v1/generate upstream=control-plane:504 "routing-policy: db timeout"
```

ron: running `kubectl get pods -n control-plane` — I see a few routing-policy replicas in CrashLoopBackOff and high mem usage on config-db sidecar. Possible DB connection pool saturation.

maya: checking control-plane metrics — auth service latency spiked ~08:10 and error rate hit 12%. routing-policy had elevated `db_query_time` and several `pg: no connections` errors.

alex: customer is in a production flow, impact is high. @ron can we do a temporary mitigation? fallback routing or scale up routing-policy?

ron: provisioning scaleups now. Increasing routing-policy replicas from 3 -> 6 and bumping config-db max_conn to 200 for the pool used by routing-policy. Applying config change now.

deploy-bot: deploy started by ron — routing-policy replicas: 3 -> 6 (deployment/routing-policy).

maya: also enabling short-term circuit-breaker: if routing-policy fails, use default-routing (fast path) to avoid full control-plane dependency. Patch applied to gateway config.

ron: applied DB pool change via `kubectl exec -n control-plane config-db-0 -- psql -c "ALTER SYSTEM SET max_connections = '200'; SELECT pg_reload_conf();"` — logs show connections freed up.

maya: after scale and circuit-breaker, error rate dropped to ~0.5% and auth latencies back to baseline. Ingress 502s gone for the last 7 minutes.

customer-acme: thanks — we see success now and throughput returning to normal. Can you confirm root cause and next steps?

maya: root cause summary: routing-policy service saturated DB pool under a sudden surge of requests (likely from a misrouted batch job). This caused auth/session lookups to time out (shared DB), which propagated 502/504s to the gateway.

maya: immediate remediation we did: 1) scaled routing-policy replicas 2) increased DB pool for routing-policy 3) enabled gateway fallback to default routing policy 4) cleared a backlog of DB connections. All reduced error surface.

alex: follow-ups: we should add a protective rate limit/quota for internal control-plane calls and add improved alerting on PG connection saturation. Also need a post-incident action: check any customer batch jobs that spiked traffic around 08:10.

ron: filing an infra ticket for permanent fix: connection pool autosizing, more robust fallbacks, and knob to route to stateless policy when DB is unhealthy. I'll attach reproducible steps.

maya: repro notes (internal): to reproduce, run a synthetic load against routing-policy with many concurrent policy evaluations while starving PG connections, e.g.:
```
# synthetic load test
ab -n 10000 -c 500 -p payload.json -T application/json https://control-plane.internal/policy/eval
# meanwhile set max_connections low to simulate saturation
kubectl exec -n control-plane config-db-0 -- psql -c "ALTER SYSTEM SET max_connections = '50'; SELECT pg_reload_conf();"
```

alex: communicated mitigation & timeline to customer. We'll follow-up with a postmortem and planned fixes.

customer-acme: appreciate the quick response. Please include any credits or SLA notes if this counts as downtime.

alex: noted — CS will follow the SLA process. Marking thread as high priority until postmortem complete. :thumbsup:
